topic: Should homework be abolished in primary schools?

turns.content: Homework in primary schools should be abolished because young children learn best through play, sleep, and family time rather than worksheets. Research on early grades consistently finds near-zero correlation between homework volume and achievement, while evening assignments generate stress, tears, and conflict that poison attitudes toward learning. Seven-year-olds already spend six hours in classrooms, and sending them home with another hour of drills leaves no room for reading for pleasure, outdoor play, or simply resting growing brains. Teachers report that much of it is busywork copied the next morning, and parents without flexible schedules cannot supervise fairly, widening inequality. Finland limits formal homework in early years yet outperforms heavier systems, suggesting class time quality matters far more. Childhood is short, and schools should protect it instead of extending the school day onto the kitchen...
